card.statement:
A simplest deformation $A+{\cal D}(\vec
{\varepsilon})$ of a square matrix $A$ is versal if there exists an $n\times n$ matrix ${\cal S}(X)$ and a neighborhood $U\subset \mathbb
C^{n\times n}$ of $0_n$ such that

- [(i)] the entries of ${\cal
      S}(X)$ are power series in variables $x_{ij}$, $i,j=1,\dots,n$ (they form the $n\times n$ matrix of unknowns $X=[x_{ij}]$),

- [(ii)] these series are convergent in $U$ and ${\cal
      S}(0_n)=I_n,$

- [(iii)] ${\cal
      S}(E)^T(A+E){\cal S}(E)\in
      A+{\cal D}(\mathbb C)$ for all $E\in U$.
card.label: Definition 2

paper.title: Miniversal deformations of matrices of bilinear forms
paper.abstract: V.I. Arnold [Russian Math. Surveys 26 (2) (1971) 29-43] constructed a miniversal deformation of matrices under similarity; that is, a simple normal form to which not only a given square matrix A but all matrices B close to it can be reduced by similarity transformations that smoothly depend on the entries of B. We construct a miniversal deformation of matrices under congruence.
